_source: The sourcing contract for the Executive Weekly Health Report. specs/exec_scorecard_rules.json says what is SCORED; this file says what must be COLLECTED for the parts nothing in the business produces yet. Nick, 2026-09-17: a list of the formats required for the data we do not have, to share with the team so we can link it to the database.
_howToRead: Each request is one thing somebody must produce. `kind` says what sort of thing: a FILE somebody exports or maintains, a COLUMN added to something that already exists, a MAPPING that is written down once, or a REGISTER that has to be created before it can be exported. `unlocks` names the factors it turns on. `columns` is the header contract — it is deliberately shaped like the dashboard's own SOURCES entries so a delivered file becomes an upload slot with no translation.

conventions._note: These hold for EVERY file below. They are the same rules the Upload Station already enforces, so a file that follows them loads on the first try.
conventions.dates: ISO, YYYY-MM-DD. Never 03/04 — that is two different days in two countries. A time goes in its own column as HH:MM (24h).
conventions.agentIdentity: The CB number, in its own column, exactly as the Agent List spells it. CB-15, CB15 and cb 15 all normalise, so any of them is fine — a NAME alone is not, because two agents share one.
conventions.headerRow: Exactly one header row, in row 1. No title banner above it, no merged cells, no colour-coded meaning, no blank spacer rows.
conventions.totals: No totals row and no subtotal rows. The report does its own arithmetic and a totals row loads as a fake record.
conventions.oneRowPer: Every file states its grain below and must hold to it — one row per thing, repeated for each thing. A row that summarises other rows breaks the load.
conventions.money: Rands, plain numbers, no R and no thousands separator. State ex or incl VAT in the column name; never leave it to be guessed.
conventions.empty: Leave a cell blank when there is no value. Never 0, never N/A, never a dash — an absence is not a nought, and the report is built to tell them apart.
conventions.naming: <REQUEST_ID>_YYYY-MM-DD.xlsx, dated for the period it describes, not the day it was exported.
conventions.delivery: Drop into the Upload Station like any other export. A request marked `newSource` needs a SOURCES entry and a TRANSFORM mapping added first — that is our job, not the sender's.
conventions.history: Send the whole register every time, not just what changed. Every one of these supersedes its own previous copy; none of them append.

requests.title: Seat & capacity plan
requests.owner: [INPUT REQUIRED — EXCO to nominate; P18 COO/Delivery Executive is vacant]
requests.grain: one row per site per shift per month
requests.why: The numerator is live — 129 active agents. The DENOMINATOR does not exist anywhere, and KB module 10 warns that forecast headcount can pass 330 physical seats unseen. Without it, capacity is unmeasurable and recruitment has nothing to size itself against.

columns.name: Month
columns.note: first day of the month the plan covers

columns.name: Shift
columns.note: a plan with one shift still names it

columns.name: Campaign
columns.note: blank = the whole floor

columns.name: Physical Seats
columns.note: desks that exist

columns.name: Support Seats
columns.note: held separately — support people occupy desks too

columns.name: Planned Productive Seats
columns.note: what the plan says should be SELLING

requests.title: Scheduled hours (the roster, not the register)
requests.system: HR OS (SYS-008, G2 red) or the WFM sheet
requests.grain: one row per agent per day
requests.cadence: weekly, Monday for the week past
requests.why: The attendance register says who was PRESENT; it never says how long they were SUPPOSED to be there. Shrinkage is the gap between the two, and it cannot be inferred from presence alone.

columns.name: Productive Hours
columns.note: on the dialler or on a call

columns.name: Offline Reason
columns.note: Training · Coaching · Meeting · Break · System down · Other

requests.title: A reason code on every agent removal
requests.system: The Agent List publish — agent_sync_logs already records WHO and WHEN
requests.fmt: one extra column on the Agent List, or a weekly leavers sheet
requests.grain: one row per agent removed
requests.why: THE SINGLE LARGEST UNMEASURED COST IN THE REPORT. Seventeen agents came off the 14 Sep list — 11.6% of the roster in a month against a 4.5% plan — and nobody can say how many resigned, were dismissed, or simply moved campaign. Removals are logged; the reason is not. One column separates a retention crisis from a reorganisation.

columns.name: Reason
columns.note: Resigned · Dismissed · Absconded · Contract ended · Campaign transfer · Promoted · Retrenched · Deceased

columns.name: Regrettable
columns.note: Yes / No — would we have kept them

requests.title: Risk register
requests.system: Does not exist. The only 'risk_register' string in the whole repo is KB prose.
requests.grain: one row per risk
requests.why: The business cannot state its own exposure. A risk with no owner and no due date is not a managed risk, it is a worry.

columns.name: Category
columns.note: Operational · Financial · Legal · People · Technology · Compliance · Reputational

columns.name: Likelihood
columns.note: Rare · Unlikely · Possible · Likely · Almost certain

columns.name: Impact
columns.note: Insignificant · Minor · Moderate · Major · Severe

columns.name: Rating
columns.note: Low · Medium · High · Critical — the matrix result, so the report never re-derives it

columns.name: Status
columns.note: Open · In progress · Closed · Accepted

requests.title: Incident register — POPIA, data and health & safety
requests.grain: one row per incident
requests.cadence: weekly, and immediately for anything severe
requests.why: The suite has POPIA CONTROLS — masking on by default, per-app login, scoped sessions — and no POPIA RECORD. A controls posture is not an incident count, and the report must never imply one from the other. Health & safety shares the file because the shape is identical and neither justifies its own process.

columns.name: Category
columns.note: Data / POPIA · Health & safety · Security · Other

columns.name: Severity
columns.note: Low · Moderate · High · Critical

columns.name: Summary
columns.example: Lead list emailed to a personal address

columns.name: Data Subjects Affected
columns.note: POPIA rows only; blank when not a data incident

columns.name: Regulator Notified
columns.note: Yes / No / Not required

columns.name: Closed
columns.note: blank while open

requests.title: Legal register — contracts and matters
requests.grain: Contracts — one row per agreement. Matters — one row per dispute or claim.
requests.cadence: monthly for contracts, weekly for matters
requests.why: Two of LRC's factors have no source at all. An employment dispute becomes a LEGAL matter here once attorneys are instructed — it is counted as discipline in Workforce until then, and never in both.

Contracts.name: Type
Contracts.note: Client · Supplier · Lease · Employment template · Other

Contracts.name: Signed
Contracts.note: blank means UNSIGNED, which is the point of the measure

Contracts.name: Status
Contracts.note: In force · Expired · In negotiation · Terminated

Matters.name: Status
Matters.note: Open · At CCMA · At court · Settled · Closed

Matters.name: Exposure Estimate (R)
Matters.note: best estimate; blank if genuinely unknown

requests.title: Blue export — tickets and actions
requests.system: Blue — already the system of record for actions; it simply does not export here
requests.grain: one row per ticket or action
requests.why: Blue already holds this. Four factors across two sections are dark for want of an export, and the KB's own governance rule — 'a red number without a Decision/Action object is not governed' — cannot be measured without it.

columns.name: Source
columns.note: Audit · Review · Council · Request · Incident — needed to separate governance actions from day-to-day tickets

columns.name: Closed
columns.note: blank while open — this is what makes backlog and ageing computable

columns.name: SLA Target (hours)
columns.note: if Blue holds it; otherwise we agree one per priority

requests.title: IT service-desk tickets
requests.system: NO TICKETING SYSTEM IS NAMED IN THE 13-SYSTEM REGISTER. A system must be chosen before it can be fed.
requests.fmt: .csv — or the same shape as BLUE_ACTIONS on an 'IT Service' board, which is the cheaper answer
requests.grain: one row per ticket
requests.why: IT service quality cannot be scored at all today; the factor leaves the denominator and the section is scored on four fifths of its weight. If IT runs on a Blue board rather than a separate tool, this request disappears into BLUE_ACTIONS.

requests.title: Dialler availability log
requests.grain: one row per outage, plus one row per day stating the shift window
requests.why: The call export proves calls HAPPENED; it can never prove the dialler was UP. A quiet hour and a dead dialler look identical in an export of calls that happened, so inferring uptime from volume would be a guess wearing a measure's clothes.

columns.name: Outage Start
columns.note: blank on a clean day — one row per day either way

requests.title: Signed monthly budget
requests.grain: one row per campaign per month
requests.why: Revenue is exact to the rand and 'revenue vs budget' is unscoreable, because there is nothing to divide it by. This is the single cheapest unlock in the whole pack: one small sheet turns 30% of the Finance section from a placeholder into a measure.

columns.name: Campaign
columns.note: use ALL for a floor-wide line

columns.name: Signed By
columns.note: an unsigned budget is a forecast and is reported as one

requests.title: General-ledger extract
requests.grain: one row per account per cost centre per month
requests.cadence: monthly, once the month is closed
requests.why: Cost per agent, seat contribution and the whole margin picture are MODEL figures from KB module 07 today — and that model carries an unresolved conflict on agent basic salary (R5,000 vs R5,250). A model is not an actual, and the report will keep saying so until this lands.

columns.name: Cost Centre
columns.note: without this, cost cannot be split by campaign and only a floor-wide figure is possible

columns.name: Class
columns.note: Direct · Support · Facility · Overhead — decides what counts in seat contribution

requests.title: Payroll run summary
requests.grain: one row per agent per month
requests.why: Two things at once. Payroll as a share of revenue is unmeasurable without it — and so is whether the commission engine is RIGHT. The projection is live and worked-example verified; what was actually paid exists in no system this report can see, so the two have never been compared.

columns.name: CB Number
columns.note: the join. An employee number alone cannot be matched to the Agent List.

columns.name: Commission Paid (R)
columns.note: this is the number the commission engine is checked against

requests.pii: Salary is the most sensitive file in this pack. It rides the same masking and the same login as everything else, and only the Finance tab ever shows a per-person row.

requests.title: Training cohorts and completions
requests.system: LMS — named in the system register, never connected
requests.grain: Cohorts — one row per learner per cohort. Completions — one row per learner per course.
requests.cadence: per intake, and weekly for completions
requests.why: Nesting PRODUCTION is already measured — it is a reported campaign. The PROGRAMME is invisible: no curriculum, no cohort, no pass mark, no graduation. 'No go-live without a training pass' is a confirmed rule with no evidence trail behind it.

Cohorts.name: CB Number
Cohorts.note: blank until a CB is issued; then it must be filled in retrospectively or the cohort cannot be followed to the floor

Cohorts.name: Pass Mark
Cohorts.note: the standard in force for that cohort

Completions.name: Required
Completions.note: Yes / No — only required courses are scored

requests.title: Training intake plan
requests.fmt: .xlsx — may be a tab on SEAT_PLAN
requests.grain: one row per month per campaign
requests.why: The nest roster is real; the number it is supposed to be is not. Half a factor is live and the other half is a plan nobody writes down.

columns.name: Planned Sales-Ready
columns.note: what the plan expects to reach the floor

requests.title: The recruitment pipeline map
requests.fmt: a short written mapping, once — not a file, not an integration
requests.grain: one line per pipeline stage
requests.cadence: once, then whenever the pipeline changes
requests.why: THE CHEAPEST UNLOCK IN THE PACK AND THE MOST MISUNDERSTOOD. Recruitment is NOT a missing integration: tools/fetch-referrals.mjs already authenticates against this exact HighLevel location with a working LeadConnector v2 client and a stored credential. What is missing is which pipeline is the recruitment one, and which stage ids mean applied / pre-screened / interview booked / interviewed / offered / accepted / started / floor-ready. That is a naming decision, and it turns on most of a section.

columns.name: Stage ID
columns.note: as GHL shows it

columns.name: Funnel Step
columns.note: Applied · Pre-screened · Interview booked · Interviewed · Offered · Accepted · Started · Floor-ready

columns.name: Calendar
columns.note: which GHL calendar holds interviews, for the show rate

columns.name: Campaign Tag Convention
columns.note: how a marketing source is tagged on a contact

requests.title: Open requisitions
requests.system: Nothing records that a seat was opened
requests.fmt: .xlsx — or a GHL pipeline of its own
requests.grain: one row per requisition
requests.why: Time to fill needs a start. The END of the measure is already in the database — a first Agent List sighting — so only the opening date is missing.

columns.name: Filled By CB
columns.note: one row per seat, or a comma list; blank while open

requests.title: System register — re-dated
requests.system: Chatterbox Operating System Governance v1.1 — a document that already exists
requests.grain: one row per registered system
requests.why: This one is not missing — it is AGEING. The register reads 13 systems, 10 red, 2 amber, 1 grey, ZERO at G4 and 27 open actions, and it is dated 2 July. The report prints that date beside the score precisely so nobody quotes July in December. Re-date it monthly and the only measured number in LRC becomes current.

columns.name: Gate
columns.note: G0 · G1 · G2 · G3 · G4 — G4 is live and controlled

columns.name: Rules Signed
columns.note: Yes / No / Not applicable — SYS-003 runs on unsigned rules today

requests.title: Facilities daily log — seats, power, connectivity
requests.owner: [INPUT REQUIRED — EXCO to nominate; P18 vacant]
requests.grain: one row per site per day
requests.why: The whole section is dark, and in Durban this is a production input rather than a facilities nicety: an uncovered load-shedding stage is dialling time the floor never gets back. Three factors come off one short daily row.

columns.name: Seats Usable
columns.note: machine, headset and login all working at shift start

columns.name: Power Outage Minutes
columns.note: within shift hours

columns.name: Power Covered Minutes
columns.note: of the above, how many the UPS or generator carried

columns.name: Shift Minutes
columns.note: the denominator — state it, never assume it

requests.title: Facilities maintenance jobs
requests.fmt: .csv — or a Blue board, which is the cheaper answer
requests.grain: one row per job
requests.why: The only facilities factor that is not on the daily log. If facilities runs on a Blue board this request disappears into BLUE_ACTIONS.

requests.title: Reporting calendar
requests.grain: one row per report per due date
requests.why: Governed reports delivered on time cannot be measured without a list of what is due and when. Small file, and it also tells this report when IT is itself late.

columns.name: Frequency
columns.note: Daily · Weekly · Monthly · Quarterly

requests.title: Marketing content calendar
requests.grain: one row per content item
requests.why: Module 09's rule is that marketing's output is measurable demand, not artwork volume — so the calendar must carry the pillar and the channel, not just a publish date, or the measure becomes a count of posts.

columns.name: Pillar
columns.note: Recruitment · Culture · Client acquisition · Leadership · Performance proof · Short video · Dashboard proof

columns.name: Campaign Tag
columns.note: the same tag GHL_PIPELINE_MAP names, so an application can be traced to the post that caused it

requests.title: Marketing and lead spend
requests.grain: one row per channel or supplier per month
requests.why: Cost per qualified lead is an estimate until spend arrives. Paired with LEAD_ATTRIBUTION it also answers which supplier is worth paying.

columns.name: Purpose
columns.note: Sales leads · Recruitment · Brand

requests.title: Lead delivery plan
requests.fmt: .xlsx — may be a tab on BUDGET
requests.grain: one row per week per campaign per supplier
requests.why: Leads arrive measurably. What they were SUPPOSED to be is a plan nobody writes down, so 'leads delivered vs plan' has a numerator and no denominator.

requests.title: A source key carried from lead to sale
requests.system: The lead load and Salesforce — both exist; the key does not survive between them
requests.fmt: one column on the lead file, preserved onto the case
requests.grain: one value per lead, carried to the case it becomes
requests.why: THE ATTRIBUTION GAP, and it is a single column. Conversion is computable in total and NOT by source, because nothing survives from the lead batch through to the booked case. Nobody can say which supplier is carrying the floor and which is being paid for nothing — while MARKETING_SPEND would tell us what each one costs. The two together are the whole lead economics question.

columns.name: Lead Source Key
columns.note: supplier + batch. It must be written onto the lead at load AND survive onto the case in Salesforce — a key that stops at the lead file answers nothing.

columns.name: Consent Evidence
columns.note: module 09: no consent evidence, no payable lead

requests.title: Insurance opt-in, published where the report can read it
requests.system: PULSE perfScore — the driver already exists and is computed
requests.fmt: an added field on the Ops digest, or a PULSE digest of its own
requests.grain: agent · month to date
requests.why: The only Performance factor the report cannot reach, and no one outside this repo needs to do anything about it. The number is real and lives in the wrong app: either the Ops engine derives opt-in from the ViciDial Insurance Opt-In disposition it already parses, or PULSE publishes a digest of its own. Everything else on that tab is already live.

columns.name: opt
columns.note: opt-ins in the period

columns.name: optPct
columns.note: against sales

_changes.why: "give a list of the formats required for the data we do not have to share with the team to source all the data so we can link it to the database". Every factor that is not fully covered now has a named request behind it, with the exact header contract, and diagnostics/verify-exec-report.mjs fails if one is left without.
